QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_14

question.text: Ms. Aarti Kulkarni is explaining to the investment committee why a Cat III AIF allocation complements a traditional equity + debt portfolio. Which combination of features BEST captures the Cat III diversification argument per the chapter?

answer.text: Identical correlation to the Nifty 50, high liquidity, zero fee drag
Guaranteed returns above the risk-free rate under SEBI (AIF) Regulations
Capital protection via government-backed corpus under the SEBI (AIF) framework
Access to short exposure and derivatives overlay for market-neutral or alpha strategies, potentially lower correlation to traditional indices, but with illiquidity and higher fee structures

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III AIFs deploy long-short, market-neutral, arbitrage and derivatives-based strategies that can deliver a different return stream from traditional long-only equity and debt portfolios. This is balanced against illiquidity and higher fee structures, supporting AIF diversification as a desirable strategy for HNIs. The Trap: Option A is internally inconsistent because AIFs carry fee drag. Option B is false because there is no SEBI-mandated return guarantee. Option C is false because there is no capital protection in the AIF framework. Note: The workbook supports Cat III long-short, market-neutral, arbitrage and derivatives-based strategies, AIF diversification for HNIs, illiquidity considerations, fee structures, and absolute-return strategies independent of broad market movements.
